subject: Science
title: Investigating a science question
objective_verbatim: Consolidate and revisit key ideas through investigation.
reading_age_est: rough ARI grade 5.16 on 863 pupil-visible words; heuristic age guide 11.16 years, not a formal reading-age test
pupil_words: plan a fair investigation, record a result and explain a limit.
success_criteria: I can name what I change and what I keep the same.
I can record what happened in a small test.
I can explain one way to make the test more dependable.

vocab.definition: a factor that can change in a test
vocab.example: The surface is our changed variable.

vocab.definition: a test that changes one key factor and keeps other key factors the same
vocab.example: We use the same toy in both runs for a fair test.

vocab.definition: what you observe or measure in a test
vocab.example: Our result is the distance the toy travelled.

vocab.definition: do the test again under the same conditions
vocab.example: We repeat each run to check our result.

retrieval.question: What should match a science claim?
retrieval.answer: An observation or result from a suitable model.

retrieval.question: Name an effect of added greenhouse gases.
retrieval.answer: They slow heat loss and add to warming.

retrieval.question: What do we keep the same in a fair test?
retrieval.answer: Key conditions apart from the one factor we change.

stages.pupil_text: Choose the question card: does surface change how far this toy goes? Point to what we will change.
stages.adult_text: Offer a predictable seat or standing spot and the first visual cue. No public test.

stages.pupil_text: Think back. Say, point or write one answer for each question.
stages.adult_text: Ask three low-stakes retrieval questions; prior coverage must be checked.

stages.pupil_text: I mark a start line. I keep the toy and launch the same. I change the surface, measure distance and repeat. Runs may still vary.
stages.adult_text: Model the full reasoning step, pre-teach four words and ask the show-me question.

stages.pupil_text: The plan has a fixed toy and start line. Add the missing launch control. Name the surface to change.
stages.adult_text: Show the part-done example, then allow paired talk before an answer. One-minute reset inside this stage.

stages.pupil_text: Everyone chooses the fair plan for comparing two surfaces.
stages.adult_text: All pupils answer the four-option hinge; use the decision rule, not a score.

stages.pupil_text: Test two runs per surface or observe. Record distance. Name what changed, stayed the same and could limit the test.
stages.adult_text: One adult supports agreed pupils, the other holds the group; swap across the week. One-minute reset inside this stage.

stages.pupil_text: Check the controls and result with a partner. Fix one label before you conclude.
stages.adult_text: Give a specific verbal comment (VF) and invite one self-edit (//) or read-back (?).

stages.pupil_text: Name the change, one control, one result and a next step.
stages.adult_text: Hear the answer and name how it changes the next example or support. One-minute reset and handoff.

worked_example.full: Change rough/smooth surface → keep toy, start and launch the same → measure distance → repeat.
worked_example.faded: Change ____ → keep toy and ____ the same → measure distance.
worked_example.removed_step: Name surface as the changed factor and a consistent launch as a control.
worked_example.fade_next: Next time give only the question; ask pupils to select the changed factor and two controls without a filled plan.

cfu.question: If I change the surface, should I also change the toy?
cfu.answer: No. Keep the toy the same.

hinge.question: A team compares carpet and vinyl using one trolley. Which plan lets them test the surface fairly?

options.text: Same push; change start and surface.
options.diagnosis: Changes the start as well as the surface, so the comparison is confounded.

options.text: Same start; change trolley and surface.
options.diagnosis: Changes the trolley as well as the surface, so the comparison is confounded.

options.text: Same surface; change trolley and push.
options.diagnosis: Keeps the surface and changes both the trolley and push; it cannot test surface effect.

options.text: Same start and push; change surface.

hinge.decision_rule: About 3 in 4 or more right → move on. Otherwise re-model with the named I-do example, then ask the parallel hinge.
hinge.parallel_hinge: A new team compares felt and foil with a sliding block. What stays the same: block and push, or surface? Answer: block and push; surface changes.

misconceptions.misconception: A fair test may change the trolley and surface together.
misconceptions.spot: Pupil chooses B, changing trolley and surface together.
misconceptions.correction: Change only the surface; keep the trolley, start and push alike.

misconceptions.misconception: Holding the surface fixed while changing trolley and push tests the surface.
misconceptions.spot: Pupil chooses C, changing trolley and push but not the surface.
misconceptions.correction: The changed surface must be the variable under test.

we_do.support: Use a visual card for toy, start mark and launch; point to the missing control.
we_do.stretch: Explain how a different launch could make a surface comparison misleading.
we_do.F: Use a visual card for toy, start mark and launch; point to the missing control.
we_do.M: Name two controls and record a result.
we_do.H: Explain how a different launch could make a surface comparison misleading.

tiers.F: Point to the factor that changes.
tiers.M: Name two controls and record a result.
tiers.H: Explain why repeat runs help and identify a method limit.

stems.F: I change the ___; I keep ___ the same.
stems.M: I changed ___ and kept ___ the same. My result was ___.
stems.H: My result suggests ___, but I would repeat ___ because ___.

tiers.go_deeper: Two runs differ. Name a reason and fix a method step.
tiers.early_finisher: Two repeats differ. Name a safe conclusion, then improve the method for the next test.

adaptations.cognition_learning: Show a three-card plan with two controls already placed, then remove one cue.
adaptations.communication_interaction: Let pupils point to the changed factor and say an M/H because sentence before recording.
adaptations.semh: Offer a predictable kit role and pause before changing stations; re-enter at the last completed step.
adaptations.sensory_physical: Use a low stable track and large ruler marks, or accept a staff-captured photo of a real measurement.
adaptations.eal: Pre-teach changed, same and result with gestures; allow home-language planning and M/H test explanation.

speaking_frames: I changed ___ and kept ___ the same. My result was ___.
My result suggests ___, but I would repeat ___ because ___.

ta_focus.i_do: Watch: one thing changes; I keep the other parts the same.
ta_focus.we_do: Which control is already on the plan? What is still missing?
ta_focus.independent: Point to your result. What did you measure without my help?

prompt_ladder: Point to the lesson’s diagram, kit or source.
Ask: What is done, and what is the next step?
Model one step, then return the next step to the pupil.
Finish one example together, then fade the help.

M.a: So toy differences do not affect comparison.
A stronger push could change distance.

H.q: What does a repeat help you check?
H.a: Whether results are similar under the same conditions.

H.q: If repeats disagree, what is a fair response?
H.a: Keep the results, check method and repeat; do not alter data.

interactions.answer_key: Surface changed; other three held the same.

items: Two runs use different start marks
Two runs use the same toy
interactions.answer_key: Fix different start marks; same toy is a valid control.

diagrams.alt: The same toy begins at the same dashed start line on two test tracks. Only the rough or smooth surface changes. Distance arrows show the result to measure; illustrated end marks are examples, not predicted measurements.
diagrams.caption: Use the same toy and start line. Change only the surface; measure distance. End marks are examples, not results.

practical.prediction: Will the toy go farther on rough or smooth paper? Give a reason.
method: Mark one start and use the same toy.
Launch twice on rough paper in the same way.
Repeat on smooth paper; change only the surface.
Compare runs and name a limit.
practical.risk: Check against the school risk assessment and CLEAPSS guidance. Keep the track low and clear; avoid raised drops and mains equipment. Do not invent or change results.
practical.pupil_risk: A launched toy may hit someone or drop off the track.
practical.pupil_safety: Keep the track low and clear. Retrieve the toy only after it stops.

facts.claim: In a controlled comparison, the changed factor is the independent variable and other key factors are held the same.
facts.source: AQA GCSE Combined Science 8464, Working Scientifically WS 2.2, 2.6, 3.5, 3.7, https://www.aqa.org.uk/subjects/science/gcse/science-8464/specification/working-scientifically

stages: Arrival (5 min): Choose the question card: does surface change how far this toy goes? Point to what we will change. Staff: Offer a predictable seat or standing spot and the first visual cue. No public test.
Starter (3 min): Think back. Say, point or write one answer for each question. Staff: Ask three low-stakes retrieval questions; prior coverage must be checked.

I Do (5 min): I mark a start line. I keep the toy and launch the same. I change the surface, measure distance and repeat. Runs may still vary. Staff: Model the full reasoning step, pre-teach four words and ask the show-me question.

We Do (7 min): The plan has a fixed toy and start line. Add the missing launch control. Name the surface to change. Staff: Show the part-done example, then allow paired talk before an answer. One-minute reset inside this stage.
We Do 2 (5 min): Everyone chooses the fair plan for comparing two surfaces. Staff: All pupils answer the four-option hinge; use the decision rule, not a score.

Independent (8 min): Test two runs per surface or observe. Record distance. Name what changed, stayed the same and could limit the test. Staff: One adult supports agreed pupils, the other holds the group; swap across the week. One-minute reset inside this stage.
Review (4 min): Check the controls and result with a partner. Fix one label before you conclude. Staff: Give a specific verbal comment (VF) and invite one self-edit (//) or read-back (?).
Exit (3 min): Name the change, one control, one result and a next step. Staff: Hear the answer and name how it changes the next example or support. One-minute reset and handoff.

if_behind.must_teach_core: Test two runs per surface or observe. Record distance. Name what changed, stayed the same and could limit the test. Preserve the individual evidence required above.
if_behind.shorten_or_merge: After a secure hinge, shorten repeated oral rehearsal. If needed, merge the exit reflection into the Arrival of Autumn 2 W07. Keep the core evidence and any safety teaching; record the change and coverage impact.
if_behind.next_lesson: Autumn 2 W07: Review and evidence autumn science (Entry Level Science / UAS).
if_behind.dependency: Pass on today’s checked understanding and unresolved hinge errors for the next starter. Do not replace incomplete individual work with a group product.

target_links.Cognition & learning: We do: Name surface as the changed factor and a consistent launch as a control. Record the pupil’s own sequencing, attention or independence target, including the prompt level needed.
target_links.Communication & interaction: Check: respond to “A team compares carpet and vinyl using one trolley. Which plan lets them test the surface fairly?” in the pupil’s agreed mode. Evidence an individual communication/turn-taking target without requiring speech.
target_links.SEMH: Arrival: Choose the question card: does surface change how far this toy goes? Point to what we will change. Use the agreed predictable start or pause/re-entry plan; evidence the pupil’s own regulation or engagement target privately.
target_links.Sensory/physical: Independent: Test two runs per surface or observe. Record distance. Name what changed, stayed the same and could limit the test. Offer the agreed accessible input, enlarged material or adapted equipment; record the pupil’s target-related access/independence, not a diagnosis.
target_links.EAL: Model/shared rehearsal: use variable, fair test, result, repeat with the actual example; allow first-language planning and oral rehearsal before the independent response. Record the agreed language target; EAL is not SEN.

planning_entry.target_recording: Capture E against the pupil's own IEDP target on the school's evidence app; the IEDP carries their EHCP-linked and Boxall targets, so one record serves every plan. Follow the pupil's IBSP where it differs from these routines.
